what_a_vector_pins._: WHAT A VECTOR MAY PIN — read this before excluding the `vector` layer of a round, and before deciding a case "cannot be a vector". Derived from THIS corpus on 2026-08-10, not declared: 228 vectors across 43 kinds.
what_a_vector_pins.the_rule: A vector is a FIXED INPUT and a DECLARED RESULT that a runner must reproduce. The input being a DOCUMENT is one case among several; the result being a VERDICT is one case among several.

It is NOT enough that the input is awkward to write down as JSON: a vector may NAME a scenario and let the runner build it from fixed seeds (form 8, see fork-visibility, which carries no input field at all). "There is no document to pin" is not a reason either — four of the forms above have none. An exclusion asserting impossibility must name WHICH of these forms the subject fails, and an existing kind that covers it refutes the exclusion.

vectors.note: CONSUMER FACE. Rounds 138/139/142 state a PRODUCER duty — what an operator must not emit. A vector cannot pin a duty, only bytes and the verdict they must produce, so what is pinned here is the duty's consumer face: the artifact the producer is forbidden to emit is REFUSED by any conforming verifier. The producer-side obligation stays in the operator suite (#124 F.5r-f/g/h), which is why the `test` layer of those rounds does not move. Frame 2 is a TWIN of frame 1, not a copy: same slot, same `prev`, DIFFERENT bytes — a producer that lost its head pointer and re-derived the interval from fresh input. A byte-identical re-publication would assert "the same document twice", which IS the head and is a different claim; the first draft of this fixture made exactly that mistake. HISTORY, kept because it is why this vector exists: before it, no vector in this corpus fed a same-slot twin to `verifyStream` at all — the whole input shape was unexercised. WHAT THIS VECTOR PINS IS THE REFUSAL, NOT THE ROUTE. Measured 2026-08-10 by removing the guards one at a time: this corpus's three refused stream inputs are caught at DIFFERENT depths — the sibling by four independent guards (duplicate `ust_id` → chronology → dangling prev → shared prev), the stale-head repeat by two (dangling prev → shared prev), and the headless frame by exactly ONE. A second implementation may refuse along any of them; requiring a particular one would pin OUR control flow instead of the protocol. The consequence for mutation testing is stated because it is not obvious: disabling any SINGLE guard leaves this vector green, so the honest control is directional — make refusal impossible and all three redden, make it unavoidable and the accepting control reddens instead.

vectors.note: Round 204, F.9.5-c.6. THIS IS WHAT A CONSTRUCTION NAME MEANS, in bytes. vectors.rule: S12.3.4/F.5a.2b an inclusion proof settles uniqueness UNDER its root; a root held in consumer configuration with no anchor coordinate supplies `R = R_t` by AXIOM, so the verdict names the basis on which currency is held
S12.3.4/F.5a.2 a verifier MUST NOT emit a map-based rung with no currency basis — with no admitted root the map branch is never entered and the identity axis falls to the floor
S14/F.5.1f a refusal carries every coordinate it MEASURED and the vocabulary that refused — the undecided case is where the reader must choose what to bring, so it may not be the one served by prose
S14/F.5.1f a refusal carries NO tier — the field a consumer branches on to proceed — and never floors an axis it did not reach: the integrity floor `invalid` is a FINDING, and inability is not guilt

S11.3/F.5s-b the ONE coordinate where suppression FORGES: a publisher that withholds its earliest epoch transitions moves the derived floor LATER, and every gap before it is reclassified as a period in which nothing was owed. Both answers must stay UNESTABLISHED, which is the protection.

S11.3/F.5s-c a publisher-supplied chain earns a CANDIDATE; the floor is ESTABLISHED only when root-ness enters from outside the publisher — here a consumer-held root, the same pattern as an admitted map root in S12.3.4

S12.3.4/F.5a.2 the anchored-authority basis needs BOTH halves: a CLOSED signed root statement admitted against the consumer's mapAuthorities, and that root proven included in the anchor substrate. The date rides from the ANCHOR — the signed claim carries no time, because a signer may not self-declare it.

S12.3.4/F.5a.1 clause 2 — admission is the CONSUMER's and never the statement's. A well-formed, correctly signed, genuinely anchored root from an authority the consumer does not hold mints nothing; otherwise an impostor runs its own map and earns the name.

§11.2 / F.9.5-c.5 (round-235) — a verifier that cannot compute the DECLARED inclusion construction withholds the ANCHOR coordinate and nothing else. The document's own verdict MUST equal what the SAME document resolves to with no proof attached, because membership-in-a-committed-root is a predicate over the TIME carrier and the identity carrier is (genesis, key log, witness) — disjoint, neither a factor of the other. The withheld coordinate MUST be reported positively: `time.status` is `unavailable` with an `unknown` member naming the reason, which is a THIRD state distinct both from a verified proof and from the `status:'none'` of a document carrying none — only this one is repaired by installing a connector.
vectors.note: Round 235 (#172). Before this round the whole verdict collapsed to INDETERMINATE, so attaching a CORRECT proof made a document verify WORSE than attaching none — measured on a live publisher whose own inclusion proof is final in Bitcoin. The path here is deliberately one the reference walk would not satisfy: a foreign construction is never walked with the reference tree, so the path must not be consulted at all, and a runner that reports `inclusion:false` here has walked a tree it was not asked to walk.

vectors.rule: S10 / F.7a.1-2 — a private partition is opaque without a disclosure; with the committed {nonce,value} it discloses, and where a key is also supplied the AEAD plaintext MUST equal canon({nonce,partition,value})
vectors.note: opaque and disclosed are the SAME verdict — a disclosure enlarges what the reader knows, never what the record earns

vectors.rule: F.7a.2 — commitment and ciphertext are two witnesses of ONE value; a well-formed decryption naming a different value is E-COMMIT, never a second opinion
vectors.note: the load-bearing case: WITHOUT the key this document reads VALID and discloses the committed value, so the divergence is visible only to the key-holder. A port that decrypts without re-deriving the commitment turns a key into an authority to assign the value, and its reader sees the same green verdict either way

vectors.rule: draft-irtf-cfrg-xchacha S2.2.1 — the XChaCha subkey derivation. This is the ONE piece of cipher arithmetic UST implements itself (the AEAD underneath is the platform`s), so it is pinned against the standard`s own vector and never against our output. A port derives the subkey however its platform allows — a real HChaCha20, or the same subtraction from a ChaCha20 keystream block — and must reach these exact 32 bytes; an implementation that is wrong here produces ciphertexts no other implementation can open, while every one of its own round-trips passes.
vectors.note: The 16 bytes here are the FIRST 16 of a 24-byte XChaCha nonce; the remaining 8 become the IETF nonce behind four zero bytes (S17 `ct` layout).

vectors.rule: F.7a.2 on the 192-bit nonce: the divergence rule is a property of the PROTOCOL, but the path to it is per-algorithm — the verifier must slice the nonce at the width `enc.alg` fixes (24 bytes here, not the MTI's 12) before it can decrypt at all. A reader using one width for every algorithm recovers no plaintext and reports E-COMMIT, reaching the RIGHT verdict here for the WRONG reason — which is why the pair is stated: without the key the divergence is invisible and the document is VALID, with it the two channels disagree and NEITHER value is disclosed.
vectors.note: The AES twin is `privacy-encrypted-channels-disagree`. Both are kept because the nonce width differs and the slicing is what a port gets wrong; the RULE is not duplicated — the reachability of it is.

vectors.rule: F clause 5 / §17 OPTIONAL — a verifier that HOLDS the key and the disclosure and cannot run the AEAD named by `enc.alg` MUST answer INDETERMINATE(unsupported_alg). It MUST NOT answer INVALID: an absent cipher is the verifier's limit, and E-COMMIT would accuse the publisher of a divergence nobody observed. The set of algorithms a build can run is DECLARED (F.7a.2, second corollary), never discovered by attempting the decryption — an absent primitive and an unauthentic tag are the same observation. The SAME document under a build implementing the algorithm verifies normally; both halves are normative, and a verifier implementing only the MTI is a conforming configuration, not a broken one.
vectors.note: The predecessor of this vector (`privacy-encrypted-alg-optional-unimplemented`, round 243) named the algorithm and carried a ciphertext that was not one, because this build could not produce a real one. Round 245 implemented XChaCha20-Poly1305 and the demonstration stopped working — which is the honest signal that it had been pinning a BUILD LIMIT while claiming to pin a protocol rule.

vectors.rule: CONTROL, and it is load-bearing: the SAME byte path admits a well-formed encrypted partition. Without it every refusal below could be the byte door refusing everything, and the four negatives would prove nothing.
privacy:"encrypted" without an `enc` block is a SHAPE defect: the mode announces a ciphertext channel and supplies none. E-MALFORMED, decided before any key exists.
An `enc.alg` outside §17 is the DOCUMENT's defect, not the verifier's limit: no conforming verifier may implement it, so the refusal is E-MALFORMED and not INDETERMINATE.
`enc.ct` is base64url by §5 string-only value model. A ciphertext that is not decodable is refused on FORM — a port that decodes leniently (standard base64, whitespace-tolerant) diverges here.

`enc` as a STRING. Carried as BYTES on purpose: a typed decoder (Go struct, serde) meets this before its object model does, and a port that silently zero-values the field would reach a DIFFERENT verdict from the same wire.
S3.1/S15 — the tier is composed from identity and time ONLY; privacy is not an input to it
vectors.note: same names, same values, same frame and key: one all-public, one carrying blinded AND encrypted. Different bytes, and the verdict must agree on the tier and on all four assurance axes. This exists because the orthogonality currently holds only by nobody having written `privacy` into the tier formula — and the tempting wrong rule ("a document with undisclosed partitions cannot be TOP") would let a READER's missing key lower a verdict the PUBLISHER earned

vectors.rule: CONTROL for the pair above: identical construction with an ordinary `key_id`. Without it, an implementation refusing every encrypted partition would satisfy both negatives.

S4.4 — the two private alternatives are SEPARATE productions and `enc` belongs to `encrypted` alone. A partition declared `blinded` carrying an `enc` block is refused at ADMISSION (E-MALFORMED), before any question of authorization: the mode declares which channels exist and a verifier states its obligations per mode, so a ciphertext under a `blinded` declaration falls under NO obligation — signed, published, examined by nobody, while the verdict truthfully reports that every channel the mode declares was checked. This document is genuine in every other respect (real signature, real commitment, real ciphertext from the reference producer); only the shape is wrong, so an implementation refusing it for any other reason is diverging.
vectors.note: Measured 2026-09-01 as a working exploit against this implementation: it verified VALID:LIGHT with `disclosed: ["kp"]`, while the ciphertext decrypts to {"reading":"9"} and the commitment binds {"reading":"5"}. Two values fixed at one instant with the record accountable for exactly one.
